title: Ten Thousand Delegates: What a Repeater Builds, What a ListView Builds, and a Budget a Test Can Hold

questions.question: A Repeater has a model of 10000 rows. How many delegates does it make?
questions.explanation: It made 10000 and all were alive.

questions.question: A ListView of height 300 and rows of 30 shows a model of 10000 rows. How many delegates?
options: About 21: the rows in view and a few beyond

questions.question: The ListView jumps to row 5000. What happens to the delegates?
options: A few new ones are made and the old ones are given up
questions.explanation: 11 more were made and 12 were alive afterwards.

questions.question: Does a ListView over 1000000 rows have more delegates than over 100?
options: No: it depends on the height of the view

questions.question: What is peak for?
options: The most delegates that existed at once, which the budget has to allow for
questions.explanation: After the jump the peak was 32 while 12 were alive.

questions.question: A delegate reports that it went when the counter shows none alive. What does the counter do?
options: Counts it as unmatched and keeps alive at nothing
questions.explanation: 2 were unmatched and alive stayed at 0.
